rawFindings.description: This PR flips three normative status declarations (README status block, constitution 'Status' section, phase-0-spec header plus the 0.0/0.1A/0.2 phase headers and the phase table) from 'Phase 0.0 reopened — scaffold pending' to 'Phases 0.0, 0.1A, 0.2 closed — durable event/recovery spine is proven (gate:0.2 green on main)'. Verified against the repository: package.json (workspace root) returns not_found at BOTH dd07fb2 and 20219bd384; LICENSE and .github/workflows/ci.yml (both explicit Phase 0.0 deliverables) return not_found at HEAD; repo-wide searches for 'gate:0.2', 'packages/events', and 'scripts/gate' match ONLY the documentation files themselves — there is no events package, no test-provider, no gate runner, and hence no command that could emit a GateReceipt. The spec's own normative rule states 'A phase is not passed by reading documents; it is passed when its gate command emits status: "passed"', and frozen constitution principle 10 says a phase gate is an executable command emitting a machine-readable GateReceipt, 'not a document-reading exercise'. The citation 'gate:0.2 green on main (dd07fb2)' is directly falsifiable in-repo: dd07fb2 is this PR's base commit and demonstrably contains no gate infrastructure (the base README itself says the scaffold 'is pending' — changed:README.md@BASE:11-14). Impact: the authoritative spec, constitution, and README now assert that 0.1B/0.3/0.4 'can proceed in parallel' on a durable spine that does not exist in this repository, and the PR deletes the previously accurate 'The next action' section (finish the Phase 0.0 scaffold), removing the only correct pointer to the actual pending work. Either the closure claims are false, or the evidence lives outside this repository — in which case the spec must not cite dd07fb2 as the commit where gate:0.2 passed.

proof.summary: Traced every claim of executable gate evidence to the repository at the cited commit (dd07fb2) and at HEAD: the workspace root, events package, gate runners, LICENSE, and CI workflow are all absent (not_found reads) and the only references to them are inside the documentation being changed. The spec's own gate rule and frozen constitution principle 10 make executable GateReceipt emission the sole closure criterion, so the closure declarations violate the repository's documented contract.

rawFindings.claim: Comment-posting errors now fail the entire triage job for every issue, not just needs_more_info/duplicate_hint issues
rawFindings.description: By removing the needs_more_info || duplicate_hint gate, the postMarkedComment call (and its propose/approve/execute/succeed ledger chain) now runs for 100% of successfully triaged issues instead of a small subset. Any failure inside this block — GitHub 403 (app lacks issue-comment permission, locked issue), secondary rate limits, 5xx — propagates out of triageIssue: the outer catch abandons the operation lease and rethrows, so the job goes to BullMQ retry/failure. In repos where triage previously completed successfully (labels applied + DB persisted), triage will now fail wholesale whenever the comment API call fails. Labels already applied are idempotent on retry and the marker prevents duplicate comments, so there is no data loss, but the failure blast radius of comment errors is expanded from a rare path to every issue, and labels/DB/telegram effects get re-executed on each retry. Consider isolating the comment step (or classifying comment failures as non-blocking) since the operation-complete marker is never written when only the comment step fails.

proof.summary: Verified at HEAD: triageOpts = repoConfig.pillars?.triage || {} (line ~240) makes auto_comment !== false default-true, so the new gate at line 358 admits every issue; the postMarkedComment/propose/succeed block has no try/catch isolation and sits inside triageIssue's outer try, whose catch abandons the lease and rethrows (verified in the 300-470 read). Previously only needs_more_info/duplicate_hint classifications entered this path.

rawFindings.claim: New test file does not cover the ambiguous-marker (result.action === "blocked") throw path
rawFindings.description: The implementation and its comments treat an ambiguous comment marker (multiple existing marker matches) as a blocking processing error that throws and retries, yet the new triage-auto-comment.test.js only asserts happy paths and config gating (auto_comment true/false, dry-run, marker scoping, footer truthfulness). There is no test that mockPostMarkedComment resolves { action: "blocked", detail: { matchCount: 2 } } and asserts the job throws and no new comment is created. Since this invariant is now load-bearing for every issue (the gate was widened), a regression here would silently duplicate comments on retries.

proof.summary: The blocked branch (triageWorker.js ~line 374-379) throws on result.action === "blocked"; the new test file contains six tests, none of which exercise a blocked result.

rawFindings.claim: Comment action lacks the findCompletedTriageAction recovery check the label path has, and its actionKey is not repo-scoped unlike the comment marker id
rawFindings.description: The label path performs a findCompletedTriageAction dedup/recovery lookup before proposing a new action (triageWorker.js ~line 253-258), but the comment path proposes a fresh add-comment action on every attempt with actionKey `triage:comment:issue:${issue.number}` (no repository.id component), even though the comment marker id is repo-scoped (`${repository.id}:${issue.number}`). With this PR running the comment path for every triaged issue, retries after a partial failure will each add a new ledger row, and if actionStateMachine enforces actionKey uniqueness globally (rather than per repoFullName/repoId), cross-repo issue-number collisions or retry conflicts could surface. The exact uniqueness semantics of propose() could not be inspected within the read budget (see unresolved context needs).

proof.summary: Static comparison of the two action paths in triageWorker.js at HEAD: label path (lines ~249-258) does findCompletedTriageAction recovery before propose; comment path (lines ~381-395) proposes unconditionally with a non-repo-scoped actionKey.
